decision_context.intended_user: Meridian Foundation CIO and investment committee
decision_context.committee_question: Should the Meridian Foundation reject, pilot, or adopt the proposed constrained ETF allocation process and, if piloted or adopted, what allocation ranges should the committee authorize?

statements.S1: The portfolio has a seven-year investment horizon and needs to be rebalanced annually.
statements.S2: The foundation wants to earn a return of CPI + 4% annually after costs over rolling five-year periods.
statements.S3: The foundation needs enough cash or eligible government securities to cover twelve months of quarterly distributions.
statements.S4: The 60% equity and 40% bond benchmark provides a reference for comparing portfolio performance rather than a required allocation.
statements.S5: The portfolio cannot use borrowing, short selling, or derivatives.
statements.S6: No single issuer can account for more than 8% of the portfolio.
statements.S7: Annual turnover cannot exceed 25% without committee approval.
statements.S8: At least 90% of the portfolio must be redeemable within five business days.
statements.S9: The foundation wants to avoid annual losses greater than 10%, but this cannot be guaranteed and the CIO has not defined how a breach would be measured or handled.
statements.S10: The CIO has not specified what the portfolio should optimize, so more information is needed before selecting the best portfolio.

original_modeling_assumption.description: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items in U.S. City Average, seasonally adjusted
original_modeling_assumption.provider: FRED with point-in-time vintage verification intended through ALFRED
original_modeling_assumption.as_of_rule: Use the ALFRED vintage available on the decision date. Record each input's observation date and availability date, and use it only when availability is on or before the decision date.

executed_analysis_methodology.series_label: CPI-U all items, U.S. city average, not seasonally adjusted
executed_analysis_methodology.source: Archived August 2026 CPI news release, Table 1

reserve.definition: cash or committee-approved daily-liquid government securities

liquidity.definition: portfolio market value reasonably saleable and settled within the stated business-day window under normal market conditions

issuer_limit.aggregation_rule: Aggregate all nonexempt securities issued by the same company; diversified funds are exempt without look-through under the Lab 13 case.

turnover.requires: current portfolio weights and their as-of date

illustrative_starting_allocation.label: Hypothetical equal-weight starting allocation for illustrative turnover analysis only; not actual Meridian holdings

risk.compliance_treatment: Always report UNRESOLVED until the CIO defines measurement and breach handling; do not include this statement in model feasibility and do not create an automatic prohibition.

costs.fund_expense_treatment: Historical adjusted-close total returns are treated as net of fund operating expenses when the provider definition confirms that treatment.
costs.transaction_cost_label: Illustrative one-way transaction-cost assumption; not an observed Meridian trading cost

benchmark.purpose: comparison portfolio; it receives a mandate verdict but is not required to pass

allocation_ranges.rule: Derive ranges only after optimization and the declared estimate, window, cost, and constraint stresses; do not create judgmental bands around one solution.

unresolved_decisions.question: What actual Meridian starting holdings and as-of date, if any, should replace the explicitly hypothetical equal-weight turnover illustration?
What observed or committee-approved trading-cost evidence, if any, should replace the illustrative 10 bps assumption?

Will the CIO approve the executed October 5, 2026 CPI methodology—August 2026 non-seasonally adjusted CPI-U from the archived BLS release published September 11, 2026—or require the original seasonally adjusted CPIAUCSL/ALFRED methodology or another convention? Until approved, the CPI methodology remains an unresolved modeling decision.
Is the S9 annual-loss statement a measurable limit, and if so, how is a breach measured and handled? Until answered it remains UNRESOLVED and outside model feasibility.
What independent evidence establishes each ETF's normal-market liquidation and settlement within five business days?

Lab_13.md states an 8% issuer limit without listing exemptions, while the Lab 13 case checker exempts cash, the U.S. Treasury, and diversified funds. Confirm that those case exemptions govern Project 2.
